observations: Photo 0 and Photo 1 show the same silver-colored electronic keyboard wrapped in plastic, placed on a concrete floor.
The keyboard has 61 keys (approximately 5 octaves, not 6 as claimed), with black and white keys in standard piano layout.
The brand 'YAMAHA' is visible in small letters on the front panel, near the left side of the keys.
The model name 'YPT-200' is visible on the right side of the keyboard, near the speaker grille.
The keyboard appears to be new or unused, still in protective plastic wrap.
There are no visible signs of damage or wear.
The photos are watermarked with 'IZUMACO INTERNATIONAL' and 'POSTED ON JIJI'.

claims.evidence: The model visible in photo 0 and photo 1 is 'YPT-200', not 'NP30'. The keyboard has 61 keys, which is 5 octaves, not 6. The term 'grand piano' is misleading as this is a portable keyboard, not a grand piano.

risks.risk: The keyboard may not be functional or may have internal defects despite appearing new.
risks.proof: A video showing the keyboard powered on, keys responding, and sound output.

risks.risk: The item may be a refurbished or used unit despite the plastic wrap.
risks.proof: Close-up of the plastic wrap and any signs of previous use or removal of the wrap.

proof_requests: Video of the keyboard powered on, playing notes, and showing the display.
Close-up of the plastic wrap to confirm it is factory-sealed.
Photo of the power adapter and any included accessories.
response.reason: The item is identified as a Yamaha YPT-200 portable keyboard, contradicting the seller's claim of an NP30 6-octave grand piano. The model and key count are clearly visible, but functionality and condition cannot be confirmed from photos alone. Proof of working condition and seal integrity is needed before pricing.
